groups.description: The company this domain is modeled on, Infotopics | Apps for Tableau, and the March 2026 Vortex Capital Partners buyout that frames the strategy horizons.

links.title: Infotopics | Apps for Tableau — home
links.relevance: The vendor's own scale claims (600 companies, 150+ countries, 30 viz extensions, 32 partners), the named customer logos and the 'AI on your terms' platform teaser.

links.relevance: The 2026 buyout entry: founded 2018, about 30 employees, Netherlands and London, two of 25 Tableau Hall of Fame Visionaries, and the AI, international growth and acquisition goals behind the 1/3/5-year horizons.

links.title: Apps for Tableau partners with Vortex Capital Partners
links.relevance: The 26 March 2026 announcement with the CEO and Vortex partner quotes and the stated intent to invest in AI applications and international scaling.

links.title: About us — Apps for Power BI
links.relevance: The company history: Tableau Gold Partner since 2011, ShowMeMore in the 2018 Tableau Conference keynote, the 2018 Innovative Solution Award, Hardenberg and London addresses and the 2022 launch of Apps for Power BI.

groups.description: The extension catalogue and the flagship products that anchor the write-back, self-service and distribution streams.

links.title: Extensions for Tableau — overview
links.relevance: The full catalogue grouped into write-back, visual storytelling, discovery and dashboard workflow tools, mirroring the product-brick subgroups, plus the 'never gets access to your data' claim.

links.title: WriteBackExtreme
links.relevance: The Enterprise-only write-back suite: Pfizer and Fraudio quotes, audit trail with rollback, SSO and role management, Windows and Linux installers and operation without internet.

links.title: SuperTables
links.relevance: The Excel-like grid behind the self-service stream: Post Holdings and Carter's quotes, saved views, server-side row model, generative fill and AI summarisation.

links.title: MailScheduler
links.relevance: Per-recipient filtered delivery to email, Microsoft Teams, Slack and network drives in PDF, CSV, PNG and Excel with API and audit trail, the basis of the distribute-reports stream.

groups.description: How the SaaS and Enterprise (self-hosted) models differ and what the IT administrator installs and operates.

links.title: Enterprise deployment explained
links.relevance: The self-hosted model: the customer controls upgrade timing, backups, monitoring and network access and obtains licence keys and downloads from a dedicated portal.

links.title: SaaS deployment explained
links.relevance: The vendor-hosted alternative with automatic updates, data access limited to what Tableau permits and no direct database connections from the extension.

links.title: ExtensionsManager installation guide
links.relevance: The central installer and admin platform for self-hosted extensions: Windows and Linux support, SSL and HTTPS requirements and minimum sizing behind the deploy-and-operate stream.

groups.description: The public plan ladder, how active users are counted and the support and portal commitments.

links.title: Pricing — Apps for Tableau
links.relevance: Free (1–5 users), Professional (up to 100 users, cloud, annual) and Enterprise (unlimited, SaaS or on-premises) plans, Enterprise-only WriteBackExtreme and MailScheduler, and the anonymous-token, rolling-12-month user count.

links.title: Support — Apps for Tableau
links.relevance: The support surfaces the support-and-enable stream models: docs.infotopics.com, FAQ, changelog, the my-appsfortableau enterprise portal, SLA, webinars, demo gallery and student licences.
